title: Distance, creator-bar, occupancy and residual opportunity atlas

purpose.statement: F2.8 no existe para matar BigTrap2. Existe para localizar DÓNDE vive la asimetría de F2.7, QUÉ objeto la produce y QUÉ residual queda explotable si la atracción de zona no es el mecanismo.

known_facts_frozen_before_run.mirror_overlap_with_other_zones_note: reported high; NOT equivalent to fraction of intraday range covered

corrections_to_informal_critique.real_is_not_closer_than_mirror: By construction d(real,anchor)=d(mirror,anchor). The naive 'closer to close' story is impossible.
corrections_to_informal_critique.overlap_is_not_occupancy: A mirror overlapping some other zone is not the same as 99.6% of the price-time range being occupied.
corrections_to_informal_critique.replication_after_mechanics: ES/NQ replication is valuable but second. 6E already has 201 formal sessions.

literature_anchors.cite: Osler, C. (2000). Support for Resistance: Technical Analysis and Intraday Exchange Rates. FRBNY Economic Policy Review.
literature_anchors.use: Compare published/selected levels against matched arbitrary levels. Measure trend interruption, not only first-touch race. Do not claim profitability.

literature_anchors.cite: Classical reflection principle / first-passage symmetry of Brownian motion.
literature_anchors.use: F2.7 already uses geometric reflection. F2.8 asks whether residual asymmetry is distance-dependent or bar-selected.

literature_anchors.cite: Large-tick microstructure: the gap between mid/last and an efficient-price/anchor can mean-revert locally even if the zone object is inert.
literature_anchors.use: Motivates creator-bar controls and near-anchor strata. Does not authorize a new OU trading model.

A_distance_landscape.question: Where in d does the race live, and is there a far-zone family worth keeping?
A_distance_landscape.note: Cuts were suggested after seeing the F2.7 distance distribution. They are an explicit post-F2.7 amendment, not a hidden original hypothesis.
A_distance_landscape.estimand: session-equal-weight mean of r_i inside each cut, HAC like F2.7

B_creator_bar_controls.question: Is the race a property of BigTrap2 zones or of the creator bar?

controls.rule: Same session, same side of close, same d, same width, creator bar without a BigTrap2 zone. If multiple, choose the closest in clock time; if still tied, choose lower bar index.
On the same creator bar, keep width and d but rotate the interval to another eligible disjoint location on the same side if it exists; otherwise mark unmatched.

B_creator_bar_controls.unmatched_policy: report match rate; do not impute; abstain contrast if match_rate < 0.40 in that cut

C_active_occupancy.question: How much of the accessible price-time field is actually occupied by live zones?
C_active_occupancy.unit: bar x tick within that bar's [low_t, high_t]
C_active_occupancy.active_definition: zone is active on bar b if created_bar < b <= removal_bar and not yet invalidated/expired
C_active_occupancy.isolated_definition: a zone whose interval does not overlap any other simultaneously active zone
C_active_occupancy.random_controls: same count, widths and lifetimes placed uniformly on the session range; 200 draws per session, seed frozen

D_residual_opportunity.question: If attraction is weak, what structured residual remains?

classes.opportunity: rare object; candidate for a small high-purity family, not a dense atlas

classes.if: effect concentrated in d<=2 and creator-bar controls match BT2
classes.opportunity: BigTrap2 as selector of reversal/continuation bars, not as a magnetic zone

classes.if: persistent uncovered ticks that later become first-passage destinations more than matched holes
classes.opportunity: anti-zone / liquidity-hole family, possibly later aVol or range residuals

classes.if: a declared cut has ci95_upper < 0 with support
Osler-style interruption exceeds matched controls even when r_i is near 0
classes.opportunity: zones as brakes, not magnets; different product than first-touch race
do not treat zones as independent observations; move to density-aware features

E_interruption_geometry.question: After first contact, does price interrupt, bounce, or continue through?

definitions.contact: first bar/tick that intersects the interval after created_bar
definitions.interrupt: within next H_int bars, price fails to close through the far side
definitions.bounce: after contact, next excursion of at least width_ticks goes back toward the creator close
definitions.through: close through the far side before bounce

decision_rules.OPEN_FAR_ZONE_FAMILY: d>=6 has ci95_lower>0, n_sessions>=30, resolved_pairs>=200, and BT2-control contrast ci95_lower>0
decision_rules.OPEN_BAR_CLASSIFIER: global or d<=2 remains positive, but BT2-control contrast is compatible with zero
decision_rules.OPEN_HOLE_FAMILY: occupancy p50>=0.50 and uncovered holes have higher later first-passage than matched random holes
decision_rules.OPEN_FADE_MIRROR: any predeclared cut has ci95_upper<0 with support gates
decision_rules.OPEN_INTERRUPTION_FAMILY: interrupt or bounce rate exceeds matched controls by session HAC ci excluding 0
decision_rules.CLOSE_ZONE_ATTRACTION: no far-zone, no BT2-over-control, no hole, no fade, no interruption edge
decision_rules.CONTINUE_AMBIGUOUS: interesting point estimate but underpowered after gates

next_after_decision.if_any_OPEN_star: write a one-family follow-up spec; do not open Z2 or PIT
next_after_decision.if_CLOSE_ZONE_ATTRACTION: keep F2.7 as geometric fact; stop treating BigTrap2 zones as magnetic objects
next_after_decision.if_CONTINUE_AMBIGUOUS: add power or another asset only for the underpowered family, not a full atlas
